history.summary: UNVERIFIED IDENTITY/FOUNDING DATE: Sri Sri Sidhi Binayak Pitha is described on travel sites as a temple dedicated to Lord Ganesha on Giri Road in Berhampur, said to be among the largest temples of Odisha with a golden-hued appearance. No reliable source documents who built it or when. NOT to be confused with the ancient Panchama Ganesh (Siddha Vinayaka) temple about 12 km away: that shrine's idol sits inside the trunk of two large ficus trees, and legend says Gajapati King Purushottama Deva of Puri (15th century) recovered the image in the hollow of Bara and Ashwattha trees on his way to conquer the Kanchi kingdom — it is one of Odisha's Pancha Ganesha Kshetras and draws around 200,000 devotees on Ganesh Chaturthi.

town_description: Berhampur (Brahmapur), in Ganjam district of southern Odisha, is the largest city of the region and is popularly known as the 'Silk City' of Odisha. It is the commercial centre of south Odisha and is famous for its biennial Thakurani Yatra, the month-long festival of its presiding deity Maa Budhi Thakurani. The city lies close to the Andhra Pradesh border and to Gopalpur-on-Sea, and is well connected by road and rail.
